\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{चौकन्ना} (caukannā)}{चौकन्ना (caukannā)}]{\hi{चौकन्ना} (caukannā) — alert, watchful}

\label{lesson:HI-C547-caukanna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for good fortune, then the Hindi for chance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चौकन्ना}}
\textbf{\hi{चौकन्ना}} — \emph{caukannā} — \textquotedblleft{}alert, watchful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{जंगल} \hi{में} \hi{हिरन} \hi{हमेशा} \hi{चौकन्ना} \hi{रहता} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jaṅgal meṁ hiran hameśā caukannā rahtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the forest a deer is always on the alert.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{चौकन्ना}} (\emph{caukannā}) is a tadbhava, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{catuṣkarṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}heard by four ears\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4630). CDIAL gives the Hindi word as \textquotedblleft{}vigilant, circumspect\textquotedblright{}: all ears.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caukannā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caukannā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Jaṅgal meṁ hiran hameśā caukannā rahtā hai.} — In the forest a deer is always on the alert.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for good fortune, then the Hindi for chance, then say \emph{caukannā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चौकन्ना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Alert, watchful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हिफ़ाज़त} (hifāzat)}{हिफ़ाज़त (hifāzat)}]{\hi{हिफ़ाज़त} (hifāzat) — safekeeping; protection}

\label{lesson:HI-C547-hifazat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for chance, then the Hindi for alert, watchful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हिफ़ाज़त}}
\textbf{\hi{हिफ़ाज़त}} — \emph{hifāzat} — \textquotedblleft{}safekeeping; protection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{गहनों} \hi{की} \hi{हिफ़ाज़त} \hi{के} \hi{लिए} \hi{हमने} \hi{एक} \hi{तिजोरी} \hi{ख़रीदी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Gahnoṁ kī hifāzat ke liye hamne ek tijorī kharīdī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We bought a safe to keep the jewellery safe.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हिफ़ाज़त}} (\emph{hifāzat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḥifāẓa}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, keeping\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{निगरानी} (nigrānī)}{निगरानी (nigrānī)}]{\hi{निगरानी} (nigrānī) — watch; supervision}

\label{lesson:HI-C547-nigrani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for alert, watchful, then the Hindi for safekeeping.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{निगरानी}}
\textbf{\hi{निगरानी}} — \emph{nigrānī} — \textquotedblleft{}watch; supervision\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पुलिस} \hi{रात} \hi{भर} \hi{गली} \hi{की} \hi{निगरानी} \hi{करती} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pulis rāt bhar galī kī nigrānī kartī hai.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{भनक} (bhanak)}{भनक (bhanak)}]{\hi{भनक} (bhanak) — an inkling; a whisper (of news)}

\label{lesson:HI-C547-bhanak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for safekeeping, then the Hindi for watch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{भनक}}
\textbf{\hi{भनक}} — \emph{bhanak} — \textquotedblleft{}an inkling; a whisper (of news)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{मुझे} \hi{उसकी} \hi{योजना} \hi{की} \hi{भनक} \hi{लग} \hi{गई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mujhe uskī yojnā kī bhanak lag gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got wind of his plan.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{भनक}} (\emph{bhanak}) is a tadbhava, inherited from \emph{*bhan}, \textquotedblleft{}hum, buzz\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 9382). CDIAL gives the Hindi word only as \textquotedblleft{}hum, buzz\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}an inkling\textquotedblright{}, news that reaches you as a faint buzz, is a later Hindi use CDIAL does not give.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhanak}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Mujhe uskī yojnā kī bhanak lag gaī.} — I got wind of his plan.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for safekeeping, then the Hindi for watch, then say \emph{bhanak} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हिदायत} (hidāyat)}{हिदायत (hidāyat)}]{\hi{हिदायत} (hidāyat) — an instruction; a word of warning}

\label{lesson:HI-C547-hidayat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for watch, then the Hindi for an inkling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हिदायत}}
\textbf{\hi{हिदायत}} — \emph{hidāyat} — \textquotedblleft{}an instruction; a word of warning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{डाक्टर} \hi{ने} \hi{मुझे} \hi{आराम} \hi{करने} \hi{की} \hi{हिदायत} \hi{दी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ḍākṭar ne mujhe ārām karne kī hidāyat dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor told me to rest.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हिदायत}} (\emph{hidāyat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{hidāya}, \textquotedblleft{}guidance\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
